app.name: Tagia
app.description: Batch-tag selected Eagle images with local AI (CPU / GPU / Auto)

app.title: Tagia
app.subtitle: Local AI batch tagging · GPU ready

tag.replaceHint: Replace removes every existing tag on each selected item and saves immediately. A snapshot is stored so you can restore the last replacement batch.
tag.replaceConfirmMsg: This will replace all existing tags on the selected items.
tag.replaceConfirmDetail:
Affected items: {{count}}

Every existing tag on these items will be removed and replaced with newly generated tags. Changes are saved immediately.
tag.replaceIrreversible: If you do not use Restore, this batch replacement cannot be reliably undone (Eagle has no batch undo for plugin tag writes).
tag.replaceSnapshotNote: A verifiable snapshot of the original tags will be saved first. Use “Restore last replaced tags” to put them back.
tag.replaceDialogFailed: Could not show the replace confirmation. Tagging stopped; no tags were changed.
tag.snapshotSaved: Saved tag snapshot ({{count}} items) for restore
tag.writeAnnotation: Also write tags to Note (safe Tagia block)
tag.writeAnnotationHint: Memo: only updates the <!-- Tagia --> block. Your other notes are kept.
tag.noSelectionDetail: Select images in Eagle, then run again.
tag.allSkipped: All selected items already tagged — skipped

setup.neededDetail:
The tagging engine is not installed or the path is invalid.
Open the Install tab to download the pinned engine and set up dependencies.

errors.gpuDetail: CUDA / GPU providers were not found in the engine environment.
errors.gpuNext: Next: Install tab → “Install GPU package”, or set Device to Auto / CPU.
errors.engineDetail: Tagging engine folder or venv is missing / invalid.
errors.engineNext: Next: Install tab → “Install all (CPU)”, or set the engine path in Settings.
errors.engineUntrusted: This engine folder is not trusted yet. Use Settings → Browse to pick the folder and confirm that Tagia may run its local Python and tagging code, or run Install all to create a Tagia-owned engine.
errors.installDetail: Python, pip, network download, or package install may have failed.
errors.installNext: Next: Install Python 3.10+, check your internet connection, then run Install all again. Git is not required.
errors.workerDetail: The background process stopped or timed out.
errors.workerNext: Next: Settings → Restart worker, then try again.
errors.genericNext: Check the log, then try Settings → Check environment.

models.eva02: EVA02 Large v3 — best quality, heavy
models.migratedLegacy: Model "{{from}}" is no longer supported (unpinned). Switched to "{{to}}".

settings.languageNote: Auto uses Eagle’s language. Manual choice is saved for this plugin only.
settings.engineHint: Pick via Browse (explicit trust required). Must contain run.py and tagger/. Tagia never auto-adopts common folders.
settings.trustEngineDetail: Tagia will run local Python and tagging code from the engine path below. Only continue if you trust this folder.
settings.trustEngineNoVenv: (venv python not found yet in tagia-runtime)
settings.trustEngineDialogFailed: Could not show the engine trust dialog. Execution blocked.
settings.trustEngineInvalid: Not a valid tagging engine folder
settings.trustEngineWillCreateRuntime: Tagia will NOT modify engine files (run.py, tagger/, or an existing venv in the engine folder). Runtime files, venv, and packages are stored only in a Tagia-owned subdirectory named tagia-runtime.
settings.trustEngineNoOverwrite: Existing same-name files in the engine folder are never overwritten. If tagia-runtime already exists and is not Tagia-owned, setup stops instead of overwriting it.
settings.trustEnginePackages: Install and CPU/GPU switching create or update only that subdirectory’s venv (pip install / uninstall). The user engine directory itself is left unchanged.
settings.trustEngineNotDeleted: The user engine folder is user-managed and will NOT be deleted when you uninstall Tagia. Uninstall removes only the Tagia-owned tagia-runtime subdirectory.
settings.trustEngineSaved: Engine trusted. Local code from this path may now run.

install.setupHint: Full setup: Windows x86_64 + CPython 3.10 only. May install Python 3.10.11 on Windows (kept after uninstall). Bundled engine + hash-locked packages (--require-hashes). Internet for packages and first model download.
install.platformUnsupported: Tagia full setup requires Windows x86_64 and CPython 3.10. macOS, Linux, and other architectures are not supported in this release.
install.consentDetail:
This will:
• Create a Tagia-owned engine folder and Python venv
• Install hash-locked packages from the internet (PyPI)
• Possibly install system Python 3.10.11 (not removed on Tagia uninstall)
• On first tagging, download pinned models from Hugging Face to the local HF cache

Image files stay on this PC for tagging. Continue?
install.consentDialogFailed: Could not show the install confirmation dialog. Setup stopped (no download or install without consent).
install.pythonAutoDetail:
No usable CPython 3.10 was found. Tagia can install Python 3.10.11 via winget (exact package/version/source) or the official python.org installer (SHA-256 + Authenticode).

Uninstalling Tagia will NOT remove this Python installation.
install.pythonAutoCancel: System Python install cancelled or confirmation unavailable. Setup stopped.
install.pythonAutoDialogFailed: Could not show the Python install confirmation dialog. Setup stopped (system Python will not be installed).
install.step1Desc: If missing (Windows): winget Python.Python.3.10 v3.10.11 (source winget) or official installer (SHA-256 + Authenticode). Not removed on Tagia uninstall.
install.step2Desc: Copy bundled vendor engine (fixed commit). Full source is in the package for review.
install.step3Desc: Create virtualenv; pip pin + full recursive lock with SHA-256 (--require-hashes)
install.destHint: Defaults to Documents/wd14-tagger-standalone. Only Tagia-created folders get an ownership marker for uninstall.
install.gpuHint: GPU needs NVIDIA + CUDA 12.x + matching cuDNN. Use “Switch to CPU” if it fails.
install.uninstallHint: Removes only the Tagia-owned directory (full engine Tagia created, or the tagia-runtime subdirectory under a user-managed engine). Recursively and permanently deleted with no undo. Does not delete system Python, Hugging Face caches, or user-managed engine files.
install.uninstallConfirmMsg: Permanently delete the listed Tagia-owned directory?
install.uninstallPermanent: The entire listed directory will be recursively and permanently deleted without undo. It is not moved to Recycle Bin / trash. There is no backup and no restore.
install.uninstallTypePrompt: Type the folder name exactly to enable deletion. Cancel is the default. Enter does not delete.
install.uninstallStep2Title: Type the folder name to delete
install.uninstallNoHfCache: Hugging Face model caches (~/.cache/huggingface) are not scanned or deleted.
install.uninstallSafetyNote: Only directories with a Tagia ownership marker and matching recorded path are deleted. Shared model caches and user-managed engines are left untouched.
install.uninstallNone: Nothing to remove (no Tagia-owned engine directory)
install.switchDialogFailed: Could not show the package-change confirmation. Nothing was installed or uninstalled.
